question: Which filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw support for host-mode agents, and should the first version cover exec-mediated filesystem access or explicitly split exec into a separate tracked boundary?
rationale: Current main only has the boolean `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, while open PRs propose incompatible public config surfaces and leave different parts of the security boundary out of scope.

options.title: Land a file-tool policy first
options.body: Choose a `tools.fs` allow/deny or roots contract for file/media/apply_patch tools, document that exec remains outside v1, and keep a separate exec boundary item open.

options.title: Require unified RWX policy
options.body: Pause file-tool-only PRs until maintainers design one policy model spanning read/write/edit/apply_patch and exec path effects.

options.title: Stay with workspaceOnly and Docker
options.body: Decline granular policy work and recommend Docker, VM, OS-user isolation, and `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` as the supported hardening path.

recommendation.title: Land a file-tool policy first
recommendation.body: Choose a `tools.fs` allow/deny or roots contract for file/media/apply_patch tools, document that exec remains outside v1, and keep a separate exec boundary item open.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent review signal on this exact issue and authored the original workspace-only guard and related policy unification.
